proposal.observation: Round 2 was rejected (0.7187 -> 0.7111): correspondence_f1@15 fell 0.492 -> 0.478 while sam_fill_rate (+0.0004) and depth_nan_ratio (0.0) were unchanged. The round-2 after-images explain why: initial_prompt_points.png is pixel-identical to the round-1 and start versions (same 10 centres at the same coordinates: 3 positive_slope, 1 negative_slope, 4 midpoint, 2 assume), so pushing oblique Hough to the permissive bound (25/80), lowering binary_threshold to 110 and raising pattern_tolerance to 14 changed nothing that reaches stage 5; detected_lines.png only gained a handful of short spurious oblique fragments (x~1000/y~2830, x~1700/y~1880, x~1600/y~2740) without producing any new pattern-matching intersection. The depth map is also identical across all three rounds. Since prompt centres and depth map are fixed, the only overlay component that actually altered the stage-5 output in both rounds is the SAM template: round 1 (1874 / 1120 / 11.5) lifted correspondence by +0.039; round 2 moved all three template values upward (1900 / 1140 / 11.8) and lost 0.0135. segmentation_results.png is otherwise stable: 10 rings, ring_count_error 0, K/B1/A1-A4/B2 sequence intact, a few thin dark unlabeled bars at ring boundaries in both rounds.
proposal.rule: d7/d8 (f_missing_lines / f_pattern_mismatch) are confirmed as insensitive to the in-bounds stage-4 controls on this scan: the prompt-centre set is invariant to Hough thresholds, maxLineGap, binary_threshold and pattern_tolerance across three rounds, matching the ontology note that the vertical-line fallback can mask oblique Hough sensitivity (p_hough_oblique priority fallback_dependent). The remaining active lever is stage_5_segmentation.f_template_mismatch / f_crop_offset via r_fix_template (segment_width, K_height, taper angle), and the two completed rounds bracket that lever: the incumbent template is a local best and the upward step overshot, so the untested downward side is probed with a step of similar size.
proposal.failure_mode: stage_5_segmentation.f_template_mismatch (template geometry slightly off the true segment size/taper, degrading SAM boundary correspondence); stage-4 f_missing_lines persists but is not addressable within bounds on this scan
proposal.rationale: Stage-1 remains locked, so unfolding is untouched. Denoising (3.60/3.85), enhancing (0.0004) and all detecting values are reset to the accepted round-1 values, because round 2 showed the stage-4 relaxation adds only spurious fragments and cannot change the prompt centres, while round 1 showed the stage-2/3 values are neutral for NaN ratio and fill rate; reverting them removes the variables that carried no signal and keeps the g007 over-gate risk closed. The single deliberate change is the SAM template. Round 1 (1874/1120/11.5) is the best measured point; round 2 (1900/1140/11.8, all three larger) was worse by 0.0135; therefore round 3 takes a step of comparable magnitude on the opposite, still untested side: segment_width 1855, K_height 1105, angle 11.3. This is a one-dimensional bracket search along the direction that has demonstrably moved correspondence_f1@15, rather than a new joint move. The improving analogy s021 (1874/1120/11.79) and the degrade analogy s028 (1952/1165/10.3, correspondence fell) are consistent with the template being close to, not above, the round-1 values. Expected outcome: correspondence_f1@15 at or above the incumbent with fill rate, ring count and NaN ratio held; if the downward side is also worse, the round-1 incumbent is confirmed as the template optimum for this scan. This is a joint overlay; no per-parameter causal effect is claimed beyond the observed bracket.
